title: The Biggest Earthquake Ever Sent a Wave Across the Whole Pacific

scenes.text: The biggest earthquake ever recorded sent a wave across the whole Pacific.
Chile, 1960. Magnitude 9.5. The coast sank six feet.
Then the ocean moved. A tsunami crossed the Pacific at over 200 miles an hour.
Fifteen hours later it hit Hawaii 35 feet high and killed 61 people. Twenty-two hours in, it reached Japan and flattened 3,000 houses.
The fault was one of the longest ever recorded. It shoved the seafloor up all at once.
One crack in the Earth. Waves on three continents.

description:
On 22 May 1960, a magnitude 9.5 earthquake struck near Valdivia, Chile, the largest ever instrumentally recorded. Parts of the coast subsided by around six feet.
The tsunami it launched crossed the Pacific at more than 200 miles an hour, reaching Hawaii about 15 hours later with a 35-foot run-up that killed 61 people in Hilo, and Japan about 22 hours later, where it destroyed almost 3,000 houses.
Have you ever felt an earthquake? Comment where you were.
first_comment: The quake left nearly two million people homeless in Chile and destroyed more than 58,000 houses. Hilo in Hawaii was hit by the third wave, not the first. Have you ever been through an earthquake?
